title: Browser Agents Don't Need Better Models. They Need Better Eyes. - Kushan Raj, Sarvam AI

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling

Browser agents are general-purpose web automation tools not tied to a specific application vertical. summary: Browser agents have seen little adoption because current infrastructure limits their ability to execute multi-step workflows, not because of inadequate models. Existing browser agents often struggle with basic tasks, taking excessive time to understand and interact with web pages. The core thesis is that models are already intelligent, but the environment provided to them is inadequate. The speaker built a browser-agent runtime that addresses this by changing the interface: what the model sees, what it can do, and what it learns from. Instead of relying on raw DOM dumps, which can be massive, or screenshots, which are limited in scope, the runtime uses a compressed markdown representation of the entire page. This allows the model to reason effectively using fewer tokens. For example, a page that would require 20,000 DOM tokens or a 1,100-token screenshot is represented in about 1,800 tokens of markdown, capturing the whole page rather than a snippet. The runtime also provides continuous, step-by-step feedback, informing the agent when new elements appear, disappear, or when a previous action failed. This enables the model to plan long sequences of tasks and self-correct. Demos highlight the runtime's effectiveness: a standard Claude implementation took two minutes and failed to download an Aadhaar or select a date on a trekking site, while the custom runtime completed both instantly using a much cheaper model. Future plans involve open-sourcing the project and exposing it as an API, website, or plugin to make browser agents widely accessible, fast, and reliable.

sections.title: Introduction and the Browser Agent Problem
sections.summary: Kushan Raj introduces his background and interest in browser agents, noting their lack of personal adoption despite being a cool concept. Using a benchmark, he shows how current browser agents struggle with basic tasks, taking 10-20 seconds just to click a start button. He hypothesizes that the models are smart, but the infrastructure around them is the issue, and proposes giving agents a better environment to plan and execute.

sections.title: Building a Better Interface and Demos
sections.summary: Raj demonstrates his custom browser-agent runtime using a much cheaper model than standard Claude. In an Aadhaar download demo, standard Claude gets stuck for two minutes scrolling and taking screenshots, while his agent completes it instantly. In a trek booking demo, Claude fails to select a date, whereas his agent succeeds immediately. He emphasizes the speed and convenience of his approach and mentions plans to open-source the project.

sections.title: Future Plans and Technical Approach
sections.summary: Raj discusses potentially offering the project as an API, website, or plugin. He explains the technical implementation: replacing 20,000-token DOM dumps or 1,100-token screenshots with a 1,800-token markdown representation that captures the entire page. He also details the step-by-step feedback system that tracks page changes, blocked clicks, and removed elements, enabling the agent to reason and plan effectively.
